statement.p: A decorative oak post is 48 inches long and is turned on a lathe so that its profile is sinusoidal as shown in the figure below.

image.shortdescription: A column that has a sinusoidal radius

description.p: figure of a column with a vertically varying outside radius. the maximum radius is r0 inches, the vertical distance between maximum radii is a0 inches, and the difference between the minimum and maximum radii is 2 inches.

statement.p: In this figure, r_0 = 4 inches and a_0 = 8 inches.
(a) Describe the surface of the post parametrically using cylindrical coordinates and the parameters s and t.
(b) Find the volume of the post.

static.solution:
(a) Let z be measured from the bottom of the post, and the center of the post be at x = 0, y = 0. The surface is the revolution surface obtained by revolving a curve extending vertically along one edge of the surface around the z axis, as suggested by the figure below.
From the measurements given, we obtain the equation of the curve x = \cos \left( \frac{\pi}{4} z \right) + 3, \qquad 0 \leq z \leq 48.
Rotating this around the z-axis, taking z=s and \theta = t as the parameters, we get the parametric equations x = (\cos \left( \frac{\pi}{4} s \right)+3)\cos t, y = (\cos \left( \frac{\pi}{4} s \right)+3)\sin t, and z = s, with 0 \leq s \leq 48, \qquad 0 \leq t \leq 2\pi.
(b) We know that the points in the curve consists of cross-sections of circles parallel to the xy plane and of radius \cos((\pi/{4})z+3). Thus, \mbox{Area of cross-section} = \pi\left(\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4}z+3\right)\right)^2 Integrating over z, we get \hbox{Volume } = \pi \int_0^{48} \left(\cos\frac{\pi}{4} z+3\right)^2 dz = \pi \int_0^{48} \left(\cos^2\frac{\pi}{4}z+6\cos\frac{\pi}{4}z +9 \right) dz = 456 \pi \mbox{ in}^3.
